title: Will robots cost us our jobs
titleChinese: 机器人会抢走我们的饭碗吗？
paragraphs: As new technology is introduced, there are many who worry about its impact on our current and future lifestyles – particularly when it comes to jobs. It is a current belief that with the rise of robotics and artificial intelligence, many people’s jobs, and therefore their livelihoods, are likely to be lost to automation.

This type of fear isn’t new. In the 19th century, the automated weaving machine was revolutionising the English textiles industry and would contribute to the Industrial Revolution. When manual workers became redundant, it sparked protests at the loss of their vocation.

Automation in the work place is nothing new. Machines have been performing menial tasks on our behalf for years, allowing us to escape the drudgery that accompanies many repetitive jobs. In fact, the International Federation of Robotics states that in manufacturing on average there are now 74 robots per 10,000 employees. That has risen from 66 in 2015.

General Manager of Digital Customer Engagement Solutions at tech firm Nuance, Bernard Louvat, believes that ‘AI is a big threat to low-skilled jobs, no question.’ He also thinks that AI chatbots will oust most call centre staff within a decade. When you consider that a large telecoms company like AT&T employs around 100,000 call centre staff, that’s a lot of people on the dole.

And that’s just one industry. A recent report from the McKinsey Global Institute, a private sector think tank, states that nearly two thirds of all jobs could have at least 30% of their activities automated by 2030.

However, McKinsey also believes that this new technology will also ‘create new occupations that do not exist today, much as technologies in the past have done.’ As the horse gave way to the car, hostlers became mechanics and mechanised manufacturing drove up wages and created more long-term roles than it destroyed. In fact, figures from the World Bank have shown that despite a 2.2 billion rise in population between 1991 and 2017, global unemployment has fallen by 0.3%.

‘It’s an evolution of work’ says Ian Barkin, co-founder of Symphony Ventures, a robotic process automation specialist. As low-skilled jobs are taken on by AI, people will need to learn new skills. ‘This calls on us to focus on up-skilling, Technology can lead to job reductions but it doesn’t have to,’ says Barkin.

Whether or not robotics and AI will leave us all jobless remains to be seen. Current views on the subject are mixed. Increased automation could indeed lead to a loss of some jobs, but at the same time is likely to create many more as new skills are required. Will they balance out? I’ll get my AI assistant to get back to you on that one.

sentences.english: It is a current belief that with the rise of robotics and artificial intelligence, many people’s jobs, and therefore their livelihoods, are likely to be lost to automation.
sentences.chinese: 目前人们普遍认为，随着机器人技术和人工智能的兴起，许多人的工作，进而他们的生计，可能会因自动化（automation）而丧失。

sentences.english: When manual workers became redundant, it sparked protests at the loss of their vocation.

sentences.chinese: 工作场所的自动化并非新鲜事物。

sentences.english: Machines have been performing menial tasks on our behalf for years, allowing us to escape the drudgery that accompanies many repetitive jobs.
sentences.chinese: 多年来，机器一直在替我们执行枯燥琐碎的（menial）任务，使我们得以摆脱许多重复性工作所带来的辛苦乏味的苦差事；单调乏味（drudgery）。

sentences.english: In fact, the International Federation of Robotics states that in manufacturing on average there are now 74 robots per 10,000 employees.
sentences.chinese: 事实上，国际机器人联合会指出，在制造业中，目前平均每10000名员工就有74台机器人。

sentences.chinese: 这一数字与2015年66台相比有所上升。

sentences.english: General Manager of Digital Customer Engagement Solutions at tech firm Nuance, Bernard Louvat, believes that ‘AI is a big threat to low-skilled jobs, no question.’
sentences.chinese: 科技公司Nuance的数字客户互动解决方案总经理伯纳德・卢瓦特（Bernard Louvat）认为，“毫无疑问，人工智能对低技能工作来说是一个巨大威胁。”

sentences.english: He also thinks that AI chatbots will oust most call centre staff within a decade.
sentences.chinese: 他还认为，人工智能聊天机器人将在十年内取代（oust）大多数呼叫中心员工。

sentences.english: When you consider that a large telecoms company like AT&T employs around 100,000 call centre staff, that’s a lot of people on the dole.
sentences.chinese: 当你想到像美国电话电报公司（AT&T）这样的大型电信公司雇佣了约10万名呼叫中心员工时，那就意味着会有很多人靠失业救济金生活。

sentences.english: And that’s just one industry.
sentences.chinese: 而这只是一个行业。

sentences.english: A recent report from the McKinsey Global Institute, a private sector think tank, states that nearly two thirds of all jobs could have at least 30% of their activities automated by 2030.
sentences.chinese: 私营企业智库麦肯锡全球研究所（McKinsey Global Institute）最近的一份报告指出，到2030年，几乎三分之二的工作至少有30%的工作内容可以实现自动化。

sentences.chinese: 然而，麦肯锡也认为，这项新技术也会“创造出如今尚不存在的新职业，就像过去的技术所做的那样”。

sentences.english: Increased automation could indeed lead to a loss of some jobs, but at the same time is likely to create many more as new skills are required.
sentences.chinese: 自动化程度的提高确实可能导致一些工作岗位的流失，但同时，由于需要新技能，也可能会创造出更多的岗位。

sentences.english: Will they balance out?
